mainEntity.name: Can AI write reliable README files and technical documentation for my software?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Treat AI-generated documentation as a draft that must match the actual software. It can create a useful README outline, setup guide, feature summary, or change log, but it may invent commands, omit prerequisites, or describe planned behavior as completed behavior.

Documentation is especially valuable when an owner is coordinating assistants, contractors, integrations, or multiple business workflows. Accurate records reduce repeated explanations and make later review easier.

Key factors:
- Whether instructions were tested from a clean setup.
- Environment variables and permissions.
- Current feature behavior and limitations.
- Examples and failure-handling steps.

Practical guidance: Ask AI to draft from the repository and approved requirements, then test every command and label unknowns clearly. Update the document whenever a workflow, integration, or approval rule changes.

Run My AI Business encourages organized, plain-language instructions for repeatable workflows and owner review.
acceptedAnswer.description: AI can create a strong first draft, but documentation may contain invented commands or outdated behavior. Test setup instructions, verify permissions and environment details, label unknowns, and update the document whenever code or workflow requirements change.
